title: Medical Hardship Liability Cap — Coverage-Loss Points
content:
Coverage-loss points are taken off a Medical Hardship award's hardship liability cap percent under the Financial Assistance Program (Charity Care) when an insurer ended the patient's coverage. Points are taken off the hardship liability cap percent — the percent of the annual household income recorded on the case at which the cap is figured — before the income is scaled at that percent, and the cap percent never goes below zero.

| Coverage-terminated liability posted on the patient's Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) accounts in the 12 whole months before the approval day | Claim of the patient billed to an insurer (Insurance Claim (Third-Party Billing)) in the 3 whole months before it | Points |
|---|---|---|
| yes | no | 2.0 |
| yes | yes | 1.0 |
| no | either | none |

For these points, a posting belongs to a span of whole months when fewer than that many whole months separate its posting date from the approval day, a whole month running from a day of one month to the same day of the next month or, when the next month has no such day, to the first day of the month after it.

**Hypothetical (approval day 2030-09-10).** A coverage-terminated liability dated 2029-09-11 is inside the 12 months; one dated 2029-09-10 is outside. A claim billed on 2030-06-11 is inside the 3 months; one billed on 2030-06-10 is outside.
